newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish parliament to debate Yilmaz policies.
newsitem.headline: Turkish parliament to debate Yilmaz policies.

text.p: The Turkish parliament is to debate the policies of new Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz's anti-Islamist government on Thursday, parliament officials said.
They said MPs would meet at 1500 (1200 GMT) for the debate, expected to last more than five hours. It sets the scene for a parliamentary confidence vote in Yilmaz's left-right coalition on Saturday.
Yilmaz, a conservative, has around a dozen more deputies on paper than he needs to win the vote in the 550-seat assembly.
The Islamists of previous prime minister Necmettin Erbakan, who resigned under army pressure last month, are the main opposition.

Yilmaz promised anti-Islamist measures, including an extension of secularist education, in his government programme read out in parliament on Monday. He also said he would speed up privatisation, despite being in partnership with a left-wing party opposed in the past to selling state assets.
